title: The Water Cycle and Weather Disturbances
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: The Water Cycle and Weather Disturbances Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Water moves through the water cycle by evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection. Weather disturbances such as low pressure areas, tropical depressions and typhoons bring strong winds and heavy rain; PAGASA warnings help people prepare. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): the water cycle, evaporation and condensation, typhoons, storm signals and staying safe. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Water moves round and round in the water cycle.
key_sub: Typhoons get their energy from warm ocean water.
body_html:
How to think about it

In the water cycle, the Sun heats water so that it evaporates into water vapor. The vapor rises, cools and condenses into clouds. Water falls as rain (precipitation) and collects in seas, rivers and the ground, and the cycle repeats.

A typhoon is a strong tropical cyclone that forms over warm ocean water. PAGASA raises Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals No. 1 to No. 5; higher numbers mean stronger winds. Typhoons can cause floods, landslides and storm surges, so families must prepare.

Example

Which process forms clouds?

Vapor cools.

Answer: condensation

Example

Signal No. 3 or No. 1: which is more dangerous?

Higher number

Answer: Signal No. 3

Common mistakes

  • Thinking clouds are made of water vapor (they are tiny droplets).
  • Thinking the eye of a typhoon is the most dangerous part.
  • Thinking a typhoon is over when the wind stops (the eye may be passing).
